items.criterion: A reviewer can find each acceptance line of CH-0001 (top option) in the recording, because each line has its own captioned step.
Each step proves its acceptance line as a user meets the command. Thus, a reviewer can confirm the line from the frame alone.
`visual.json` is a terminal script that anyone can record again from the project root, and the script ends with a step that runs all checks.
The change folder holds `review.gif` and its frames from a successful recording of the final `visual.json`.
The run looks at the recorded frames itself before the commit, and the run records again when a frame is wrong.
The run changes only the records of the visual review. The app, the checks, the specs, and the statuses stay as they were.
The handoff to `/pdlc:verify` obeys the template. The handoff tells what the GIF shows, frame by frame, and gives the count of acceptance lines shown.
One commit, `Visual review CH-0001`, holds all the files of the visual review, with the trailers `Intent`, `Change`, and `Review`.
The final reply tells the user that `/pdlc:verify` is next.
The user and the `verify` stage get a true account of the recording. Each claim in the final reply and in the handoff agrees with the files.
